title: How computers work, from switches up
about: Crash Course Computer Science's first seven episodes as one track, with a hands-on detour into building logic gates from transistors.
description: A branching path from the abacus to the CPU with Crash Course Computer Science, plus Ben Eater's breadboard build of logic gates as a go-deeper side path.

track.title: Early computing
track.note: From the abacus to punch-card tabulating machines: why computing was mechanised in the first place.

track.title: Electronic computing
track.note: Relays, vacuum tubes and transistors: switches that got faster and smaller.

track.title: Boolean logic and logic gates
track.note: AND, OR and NOT, built from those switches.

deeper.title: Making logic gates from transistors (Ben Eater)
deeper.note: The same gates, built for real on a breadboard.

track.title: Representing numbers and letters with binary
track.note: How ones and zeros stand for numbers, text and everything else.

track.title: How computers calculate: the ALU
track.note: Logic gates combined into a circuit that adds.

track.title: Registers and RAM
track.note: Memory: circuits that hold a value until you change it.

track.title: The central processing unit (CPU)
track.note: Everything so far, working together to run instructions.
